issues.title: The coefficient normalization does not exclude zero covariance modes

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $Q$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions $\{f_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$, spanning $\mathcal{L}^2(\mathcal{D})$, with corresponding eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$

issues.failure_explanation: A covariance operator may have zero eigenvalues; Q=0 already satisfies the old eigenbasis clauses. For such a mode, 1/sqrt(lambda_k) is undefined, so the lemma does not define omega_k for every k as claimed. This defect is independent of whether the A- and Q-eigenbases coincide.
issues.overall_effect: The coefficient lemma and its use in the general spectral proof are not well-defined for degenerate covariance operators, including the zero modes admitted by the old assumptions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the coefficient identity for every mode first in the unnormalised form using B_k(t)=⟨W_Q(t),e_k⟩. In the joint-eigenbasis setting, use the normalised Wiener process only when λ_k>0, and state that λ_k=0 implies B_k≡0 and c_k≡0. Zero modes then contribute nothing to the spectral-error sum.
issues.why_classification: The division by zero is a genuine mathematical defect, not a transcription error. However, a routine zero-mode case split removes it without excluding degenerate covariance operators and leaves the coefficient representation, spectral theorem, rate, and constants for nonzero modes unchanged.

issues.title: Coefficient coordinates are not standard Wiener processes without a joint eigenbasis

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $e_k = f_k$ for all $k$, i.e., $A$ and $Q$ have a joint basis of eigenfunctions.
If we further assume that \Cref{assumption:operator}(iii) holds, then the $\{\omega_k(t)\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$'s are independent.

issues.failure_explanation: Under only parts (i)-(ii), the covariance is E[omega_k(t)omega_j(s)]=min(t,s)<Qe_k,e_j>/sqrt(lambda_k lambda_j), which need not equal min(t,s)delta_kj. Thus the lemma's claim that the omega_k are standard Wiener processes, and temporal estimates that use them as such, are not established. The joint-eigenbasis condition makes Qe_k=lambda_k e_k and restores the calculation.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false for separately diagonalizable A and Q, and the scalar temporal results lack the claimed normalization in that broader regime. Results applying the lemma only under the full joint-basis assumption are not affected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each A-eigenvector define q_k=⟨Qe_k,e_k⟩. When q_k>0, normalise ⟨W_Q,e_k⟩ by √q_k and use √q_k in the coefficient formula and its scalar temporal estimates; when q_k=0, treat the coefficient as identically zero. Assert independence only under the joint-eigenbasis condition, where q_k=λ_k.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes an invalid covariance-normalisation inference, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the directional-variance correction follows from a one-line covariance calculation and propagates locally through the scalar temporal theorem and corollaries, preserving the non-joint-basis regime, the method, and all temporal rates without a new lemma or proof architecture.

issues.title: The Laplacian corollary violates the covariance-spectrum ordering hypothesis

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are indexed so that they are non-decreasing in $k$.

issues.failure_explanation: For beta>0 and non-decreasing Laplacian eigenvalues xi_k, lambda_k=sigma r^{-gamma}(kappa^2+xi_k)^{-beta} is non-increasing. It therefore does not satisfy the old requirement that lambda_k be non-decreasing. More generally, a positive non-decreasing sequence cannot be bounded above by C_2 k^{r_lambda} with r_lambda<0. The proof consequently invokes the general spectral theorem outside its stated hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised positive decaying covariance models are not covered by the old assumption, so the Laplacian application is unproved and the main theorem's simultaneous positivity and full-assumption regime is empty until the ordering is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “non-decreasing” by “non-increasing” in the indexing condition for the covariance eigenvalues. No proof or bound otherwise needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The old source itself uniquely forces the correction: covariance eigenvalues are nonnegative, the assumed upper rate has negative exponent, and the displayed Laplacian model is explicitly decreasing. The proofs already use the decaying indexing, so the wrong ordering word is transcriptional rather than a mathematical argument requiring repair.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: where the eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are indexed so that they are non-increasing in $k$.

issues.title: The Laplacian spectral bound uses incorrect powers of the Weyl constant
issues.failure_explanation: From xi_k>=C_Delta k^{2/d}, the eigenvalues satisfy mu_k>=r^{-1}C_Delta^alpha k^{2alpha/d} and lambda_k<=sigma r^{-gamma}C_Delta^{-beta}k^{-2beta/d}. Substitution into the general theorem gives the factor C_Delta^{-beta-(2gamma-1)alpha}=C_Delta^{-(nu+d/2)}, not C_Delta^{2-2gamma}.
issues.overall_effect: The spectral convergence exponent is unchanged, but the explicit error constant in the Laplacian corollary is not supported by its proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use C_1=r^{-1}C_Δ^α and C_2=σr^{-γ}C_Δ^{-β} in the application of the general spectral theorem. Accordingly replace the corollary’s Weyl-constant factor by C_Δ^{-β-(2γ-1)α}=C_Δ^{-(ν+d/2)}.
issues.why_classification: The proof applies powers incorrectly when deriving its eigenvalue bounds, so an algebraic inference and the stated constant must be corrected. The repair is short and routine, requires no new result, and leaves the convergence exponent, hypotheses, and substantive guarantee unchanged.

issues.title: The temporal theorem applies the projection outside its declared domain

failure_location.quote: for all $h: [0,t) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ of the form $h(s) = g(s) + \alpha f_t(s)$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We then assume that we have a map $\Pi_m: \mathcal{L}^2([0,T]) \supset \mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{P}_m(\mathcal{I})$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims an error bound for the estimator Pi_m f_t, but the inherited operator has domain A contained in L2([0,T]), whereas f_t and the functions g+alpha f_t used in the theorem are specified only on [0,t). For t<T and general fractional gamma, extending the real power to s>t is not defined, and no alternative extension or extension-independence property is supplied. Thus the estimator and the theorem's boundedness hypothesis are ill-typed.
issues.overall_effect: The generic temporal estimator and the formal results derived from it are not well-defined under the declared operator interface, although the concrete methods and all proof norms naturally use the local interval [0,t).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each fixed t, define the projection on L²([0,t)) and define its piecewise-polynomial codomain using the mesh intervals restricted to [0,t). Use this local-domain interpretation consistently in the temporal theorem, its corollaries, and the full-discretisation theorem.
issues.why_classification: The old theorem, concrete projection, estimator, and every proof norm consistently operate on [0,t), uniquely determining the intended interface. Correcting the copied [0,T] domain is an ill-typed-object correction; it changes no construction, estimate, rate, or applicability.

issues.title: The order-zero corollary retains an unsubstituted method order

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the temporal part of the error converges like $h^{\min(2\gamma - 1, 2)}$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose, notation c_k^(0), and piecewise-constant operator all fix m=0. The general exponent min(2gamma-1,2m+2) therefore becomes min(2gamma-1,2). The one-line proof supports that specialized rate, not the old display containing an unquantified m.
issues.overall_effect: The old corollary does not state a definite order-zero rate and can appear to promise higher orders depending on an undefined parameter, although the later discussion gives the correct exponent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Substitute m=0 in the displayed error exponent, replacing h^{min(2γ−1,2m+2)} by h^{min(2γ−1,2)}.
issues.why_classification: The piecewise-constant operator, the superscript (0), and the ensuing prose all uniquely fix m=0, while the proof is already the m=0 specialization of the general theorem. The remaining m is a direct failure to substitute, with no mathematical argument to repair.

issues.title: The concrete high-order discretisation projects the wrong kernel
issues.failure_explanation: The executable coefficient definition projects (t-s)^gamma, while the stochastic convolution and analyzed estimator require (t-s)^{gamma-1}. No other factor in the displayed sum differentiates the projected polynomial to compensate for this change, so the formula computes a different stochastic integral and is not the method covered by the temporal error analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The concrete high-order simulation formula does not implement the analyzed projection method and therefore cannot claim its stated temporal convergence rate. The separately defined generic estimator and formal convergence theorem use the correct kernel.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the coefficients b_{ℓ,j} using the projection of (t−·)^{γ−1}, rather than (t−·)^γ, on each interval; make the same exponent correction in the accompanying description of the high-order method.
issues.why_classification: The stochastic-convolution formula, generic estimator, and projection-computation lemma all uniquely require the γ−1 kernel, and no differentiation or other compensating operation appears in the executable formula. Thus the isolated exponent is transcriptional; correcting it immediately recovers the already analysed algorithm and rate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: We then approximate the coefficient processes $c_k(t)$ by replacing $(t-s)^{\gamma - 1}$ in (\ref{eq:coefficient-integral}) by a piecewise polynomial $p_t(s)$

issues.title: The advertised inverse smoothness parametrisation omits a factor two
issues.failure_explanation: The words “or alternatively” claim that the ensuing formulas invert the preceding parametrisation. The old forward definitions and beta*=nu_s/(nu_s+d/2) actually establish 2 alpha nu_t=nu_s min(1,beta_s/beta*), so the inverse must use alpha=nu_s/(2nu_t) min(1,beta_s/beta*). The old formula gives twice that value and therefore does not recover the advertised smoothness parameters.
issues.overall_effect: Parameter choices made through the advertised inverse map use the wrong alpha and hence the wrong spatial operator and smoothness balance. The convergence theory expressed directly in alpha, beta, and gamma is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inverse formula for α by α=(ν_s/(2ν_t)) min(1,β_s/β*), leaving the other inverse formulas unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The forward parametrisation directly gives 2αν_t=ν_s min(1,β_s/β*), and the old numerical parameter choices also use the factor 1/2. The correction is therefore uniquely forced by the old source and restores the claimed inverse map without changing the model class or any convergence result.
